neighbours.label: soldiers or service members being away from home at war (deployed, overseas, far away in combat)
fire: Her husband was deployed to Iraq for a year, so she raised the kids alone.
During the war, most of the young men in the village left for the front.
The children wrote letters every week to their father serving overseas.
Families of troops stationed abroad gathered for a holiday video call.
While her son was posted to Afghanistan, she kept his room exactly as it was.
The town knitted socks for its boys fighting in France.
Spouses of deployed sailors meet every Thursday at the base chapel.
He missed his daughter's birth because his unit was sent to Korea.
quiet: Her husband was promoted to manager last year, so she raised the kids alone.
During the summer, most of the young men in the village worked on the farms.
The children wrote letters every week to their father in the hospital.
Families of the school's teachers gathered for a holiday dinner.
While her son was studying in Boston, she kept his room exactly as it was.
The town knitted socks for its children starting school in September.
Spouses of the hospital nurses meet every Thursday at the chapel.
He missed his daughter's birth because his flight was delayed in Denver.
